title: The Satoshi Protocol — Act 1: Chapter 1
description: Opening chapter: Elias in Berlin, rebuilt through breaking, before the world pulls him back in
common_context:
Protagonist: Elias Reed, 36-38. Former NSA cryptographer, burned out and hiding in Berlin for 2-3 years. Rebuilt through breaking/parkour. Lean, fluid, precise movement. Guarded, perceptive, dry wit. Pattern-sight dormant. Avoidance is his flaw — runs from what he fears.

Physical: Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) onset during the catastrophic mistake period — the body refused to carry what he was being asked to carry. Misdiagnosed as posture/screen time, year of failed physio. Breaking recovered ~90%; last 10% is stress-responsive. Shoulder tightens under pressure, loosens in flow state. Running body barometer. Never explicitly linked to Atlas/Prometheus — subtext only.

Key line to seed (use variants, not verbatim): 'The body was a system he'd learnt to trust.' The word 'learnt' matters — it embeds the journey. Never write 'you could trust.'

World: Near-future (~10 years ahead). Surveillance ambient. Corporate infrastructure fortress-like. Street level clings to analogue. Cities at night: neon, sodium, LED, cold air.

Crew (named, recurring): Leon Amari (45, French-Algerian, mentor, flow philosophy), Katya Markovic (23, Serbian, fierce, non-romantic little sister), Dominik Voss (32, German, precision, fixer with mysterious arrangement for the space).

Crew extras (ambient, sparingly used): Papa (crew elder, past caring what others think, does full handshake round every session — nod/fist-bump/full-dap-with-finger-flick hierarchy, gives Elias a hand on the shoulder instead of a dap, never explained). Felix (the New Guy, enthusiastically annoying, wipes his face too often, wants into every conversation). Wider international crew as background only: Bhutanese pair, Glasgow blow-in, Lisbon regular, Polish top-rocker, Japanese exchange student.

Breaker culture rules: NO chalk (they need palms to slide). Water sip as reset ritual. Breakers are naturally shy/introverted — default to battle mode around strangers. Papa's handshake discipline is cultural work against this default.

Tone: Third person limited, past tense, close distance. le Carre intimacy + Gibson texture. Technical precision, controlled emotion. The walls are part of the architecture.

Music rule: Load-bearing scarcity. Maximum ONE named track per scene. All other music described sensorially, no credits. Never write a playlist.

Core rule: Never stop plot to explain. Embed ideas in action, dialogue, and subtext.

slots.scene_context:
POV: Elias, third limited, past tense, close distance.
Cast: Elias, Leon, Katya, Dominik, Papa (crew elder), Felix (New Guy), international background crew (Bhutanese pair, Glasgow blow-in, others — populate sparingly).
Pacing: warm, rhythmic, grounded. Opening calm — establish before disturbing.
Length: tight. Target ~4500 chars. Resist interior drift — show through action, not reflection.
Integrate: breaking as flow state / body as a system Elias has LEARNT to trust. Shoulder as running physical tell. Personal proof of work.
Music pivot: ONE named track only — 'Don't Sweat the Technique' (Eric B. & Rakim) lands precisely as Elias commits early and nails the precision landing he's been fumbling. Title becomes the action. Before and after: ambient funk break, described sensorially with no credits. Leon changes track to DUB at session end — silent decree that the session is over. Katya reacts to dub by leaving fast.
Ritual: NO CHALK. Water bottle sip as reset. Greeting hierarchy: nod / fist bump / full dap with finger-flick. Papa does the full round; gives Elias a hand on the shoulder instead.

Evening session at the crew's Berlin training space. Elias in the circle, working his sequence. Establish the found family, the rebuilt life, the peace that may or may not be real. Session winds down when Leon changes the music.
slots.setting: Industrial training space in Berlin. Light-industrial unit before whatever it was before that — layers of use written into the walls. Exposed brick buried under graffiti buried under newer graffiti, oldest tags geological, colours bled into the mortar. Ceiling goes up seven metres and is lost in shadow past the reach of the yellow work lights Dominik has arranged on tripod stands in a rough perimeter. Marked zone taped on the concrete floor for the cipher. Portable speaker at the edge, Leon's rotation playing. Water bottles scattered. Layers of clothing stacked against the wall. Cold outside — Berlin November that comes in like a landlord. Inside, the heat is bodies and movement. The concrete is cold under bare palms anyway.
slots.character_action: Elias works his sequence — a flow through a jump to a precision to a wall-run to a controlled fall. Deliberately shoulder-friendly choices. The precision landing has a half-beat of hesitation in it he can't train out — the body protecting the joint without asking his mind first. Katya attempts a freeze, fails, hits the concrete shoulder-first, rolls up laughing. She walks to her water bottle, takes a sharp sip, resets, tries again. Lands it. Walks away without celebrating. Dominik drills a wall-run with mechanical patience — trying to encode it through repetition, the way he does everything. Leon stands against the east wall with a Glasgow blow-in deep in conversation, hands moving as he talks — but his eyes flick to Elias mid-sequence and he catches the half-beat hesitation without breaking the conversation. Felix (the New Guy) wipes his face too often and tries to insert himself into Dominik's drilling — gets a polite half-acknowledgment that would crush a more self-aware man. Papa arrives partway through the session and begins his round — full dap with finger-flick follow-through for the Bhutanese pair, a nod for Dominik, a fist bump for Katya that she returns without stopping her next sequence. When Papa reaches Elias, he puts a hand on Elias's shoulder instead of the ritual. Nothing said. Moves on.
slots.dialogue:
Katya, resetting at her water bottle after the first failed freeze: 'You're watching again. Either join or coach — standing there is creepy.' Elias: 'Your left arm is doing all the work. Let the hip carry it.' She doesn't thank him — just goes back and lands it.

Later, Leon calling across the space without looking, mid-conversation with the blow-in: 'Half-beat late on the precision, Elias. Same one as yesterday.' Then he returns to his conversation as if he hasn't spoken.

Papa's arrival is mostly not words — just the greetings. The handshake hierarchy playing out in silence. When he reaches Felix, who tries to start a conversation, Papa gives him a fist bump and moves on without breaking stride.
slots.internal: What happened when he moved well was that everything else stopped. That was the discovery that had kept him here three years past the point where he'd planned to leave — the silence that lived inside the right movement. The body was a system he'd learnt to trust. The word learnt mattered. It had not come naturally. It had not come fast. There had been a year when the body had refused him entirely — when he'd woken one morning unable to lift his arm past his collarbone, and three physios had told him it was posture, or screen time, or stress, and none of them had been right or wrong in a way that mattered. Breaking had done what the exercises hadn't. The shoulder was tight today, a low whisper of old adhesion, manageable but present — and by the third pass through the sequence it had loosened into background. Flow state quieted the joint before the mind caught up.
slots.tension: No external threat. The tension is internal and quiet — this peace is built on avoidance. A man hiding in plain sight, and every easy evening is borrowed time he hasn't earned. The shoulder knows before the mind does. And Papa — walking his round, dispensing the full ritual to everyone else and a silent hand to Elias — Papa knows, or intuits, or has simply seen enough burnt-out men to recognise one. Elias doesn't examine the shoulder touch. He never does.
slots.sensory: Kick and snare through the floor — an old funk break, unnamed, the foundation Leon's rotation always started on. Chalk dust absent — breakers don't chalk — but the air carries the particular dryness of a room where bodies have been working. The shock of cold concrete against his palms on the wall-run entry (shoulder holds). Katya's sharp exhale as she resets. The geological layers of graffiti in the periphery, the oldest tags bled into the mortar like sediment. Then — precisely as Elias commits early and lands the precision clean — the speaker cycles into 'Don't Sweat the Technique,' Rakim's voice dropping in exactly as the weight transfers through the landing. Title as action. He doesn't notice it consciously. The body does.
slots.transition: Later: Leon walks to the speaker, changes the track. Dub drops — reverb-heavy, bass dragged through echo chambers, the kind of track Leon put on when the session was over whether anyone acknowledged it or not. Katya's whole body reacts within three seconds — shoulders rolling back, bag picked up faster than usual, a sharp word in Serbian to Leon that he acknowledges with a nod. She's gone inside a minute. The others peel off in twos and threes. Dominik leaves with three regulars, his voice already sliding into the event-promoter register. Felix tries one last attempt at Dominik's attention and gets a practiced brush-off. The Bhutanese pair bow slightly to Papa on the way out. Papa himself leaves last after his exit round. Elias stays. Leon stays. The dub carries them into the after-hours quiet.

slots.scene_context:
POV: Elias, third limited, past tense, close distance.
Cast: Elias, Leon.
Pacing: quiet, easy, undercurrent of something unspoken.
Length: tight. Target ~1500 chars.
Integrate: the mutual privacy between Elias and Leon as an act of generosity with limits. Shoulder continues to loosen.
Music: unnamed dub still playing low. Don't describe it again — it's just the room now.

Post-session. Space emptied out. Elias and Leon lingering. Establish Leon's mentorship and Elias's guardedness. Seed that Elias has a past he doesn't discuss and Leon doesn't ask — but neither is unaware.
slots.setting: Same training space, emptied. Overhead lights half-killed — just the strip nearest the door. Mats stacked against the wall. Two water bottles on the floor between them. The space feels bigger without the crew in it.
slots.character_action: Leon stretches in silence — slow, deliberate, the routine of a body that's done this for decades. Elias sits against the wall, legs extended. Rolls the shoulder once, slowly — habit more than need now. Neither is in a hurry to leave.
slots.dialogue: Leon says little. What he says lands. A comment about flow, about not forcing patterns. Elias responds with a half-joke that deflects. Leon lets the deflection stand. The unspoken rule: you show up, you train, you earn your place. No credentials. No clearances. No past.
slots.internal: Leon never asked where Elias came from. That was the rule. Elias liked the rule. He wondered sometimes if Leon had a rule like that for his own reasons — twenty years in Berlin and nobody knew what had happened in those years between Marseille and here. The dub in the background was the sound of Leon's decision-making: when the track changed, the session was over. Three years and Elias had only figured out the signal six months ago.
slots.tension: The unspoken question beneath the easy silence: how long can this last? Leon sees more than he says. Elias knows this. The mutual privacy is an act of generosity, not ignorance — and generosity has limits. Papa's hand on the shoulder earlier was in the same category. Things people know without saying.
slots.sensory: The dub running low through the speaker — bass and reverb, patient, unhurried. The building settling. Their voices in the empty space when they speak. Street noise filtering through a cracked window — tram, distant club bass, someone's bicycle bell.
slots.transition: Leon stands. 'Thursday.' Not a question. Elias nods. Leon pulls on his jacket and walks out without looking back. The door echoes. Elias sits in the quiet for another minute. Then follows.

slots.scene_context:
POV: Elias, third limited, past tense, close distance.
Cast: Elias (alone). Background: Berlin at night. Brief exchange with the Turkish corner-shop owner.
Pacing: contemplative, edge of melancholy. The peace is real but fragile.
Length: tight. Target ~1500 chars.
Integrate: surveillance as ambient weather — not dystopian, just present. Digital shadows. Shoulder reaction to cold air.
No named music in this scene. Street sounds only.

Elias walks home through Berlin. Establish his daily life, his neighbourhood, his careful ordinariness. Seed the surveillance texture of the world. End on the dark phone as the closing image.
slots.setting: Berlin streets at night. Sodium lights on wet pavement. A Turkish corner shop still open — warm yellow interior against the cold street. Graffiti layered deep on every surface, tags over stickers over political stencils. The distant blue glow of an S-Bahn platform. Security cameras on every third building — he notices them without meaning to.
slots.character_action: He walks a route he knows. Checks reflections in window glass — old habit, not conscious. The shoulder tightens a half-inch against the cold after the warm training space; he rolls it and the ache eases. He stops at the corner shop, buys black tea for tomorrow and a coffee for now. Makes small talk in passable German. A normal man doing normal things.
slots.dialogue: The corner shop owner: 'Late again, my friend. One day you tell me what you do at night.' Elias: 'I dance.' The owner laughs. Elias smiles. It's not a lie — it's just not the whole answer.
slots.internal: Three years and he still checked reflections. Window glass, phone screens, the chrome on coffee machines. Looking for the face behind him that wasn't there yet. He used to think in systems. Now he thought in movements. Cleaner. Simpler. The body lied less than the mind did, once it had finished refusing him and started cooperating again. He'd learnt that the hard way. He was trying not to forget.
slots.tension: The cameras he clocks without trying. The phone he hasn't checked. The life he left behind that left marks he can feel but can't name. The shoulder as weather vane — loose tonight, manageable, almost gone. Almost. Peace built on a burial, and burials only hold if nobody digs.
slots.sensory: Wet cobblestones underfoot. The hiss of a tram passing. Neon from a late-night kebab shop. Cold air on his face after the warm training space. His own breath visible. The weight of the grocery bag against his thigh. The small heat of the takeaway cup through his glove.
slots.transition: He reached his building. Climbed the stairs slowly, favouring the shoulder out of old caution. Inside, he set the coffee and the tea on the kitchen counter. Didn't check his phone — hadn't in weeks. The phone sat on the counter beside the tea, dark, patient, waiting for something he'd promised himself would never come.
